sections.label: Whose move it is
sections.html:
I run several Claude Code sessions at once in T3 Code. The board sits docked beside it and groups them by who has to act next, not by project.

Sessions waiting on me collect in Needs you. My own tickets, where I spend most of the day, get their own My work lane, with a stage rail from Plan to Merge on each card. Reviews holds pull requests that ask for my review, and once I’ve left feedback a review waits on its author without me checking. Start next, Parked and Done today round it out.

sections.label: Acting from the card
sections.html:
Opening a session’s chat in T3 is what I do most, so it’s one click on the selected card, next to its main action and Details: the agent’s last reply, one-tap answers and a reply box. Pull requests open on T3’s Pull requests page, and snoozes sync to T3.

Actions are tiered by risk. Safe ones run on click, and anything that changes something outside the board asks first.

sections.label: Ground rules
sections.html:
The board itself spends no model tokens, and the few buttons that start an agent are marked. It polls GitHub for review requests, refreshes whenever the window wakes, and each morning my daily-recap skill turns Done today into a recap.

Its look borrows from this site’s storefront style, and a one-click, 20-second tour shows it off.
